# Manage Harvest API credentials permissions

Access the latest version of Harvest API documentation at [**harvestdocs.greenhouse.io**](http://harvestdocs.greenhouse.io).

Harvest API v1/v2 access is being retired. Migrate existing custom integrations to Harvest v3 by your organization’s applicable cutoff date. After the cutoff date, v1/v2 API keys won’t be accessible and integrations using v1/v2 will stop working. Develop all new integrations with Harvest v3.

Greenhouse Recruiting's [Harvest API](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029266032) allows organizations to grant internal developers and third-party integrations access to data such as jobs, candidates, interviews, and offers.

Access to Harvest API is controlled through API credentials. Site Admins can assign permissions to specific endpoints or scopes, limit usage to trusted IP addresses, and revoke/re-enable credentials as needed.

### Create new Harvest API credentials

To create a new Harvest API credential, click the **Configure** icon ![Configure icon](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/article_attachments/45999126074523) on your navigation bar, then click **Dev Center** on the left.

![Screenshot of Dev Center Navigation](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/article_attachments/45999107289755)

Click **API Credential Management**.

![The Dev Center page shows API Credential Management highlighted in marigold in the middle of the page](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/article_attachments/14514232149019)

Click **Create new API credentials.**

![](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/article_attachments/48269408770459)

Make the following selections:

- **API type**: Choose *Harvest* or* Harvest v3 (OAuth)*
- **Partner**: Select the name of the integration that requested the API credential. If the integration isn't listed, select unlisted vendor. If you're creating a custom integration, select custom.
- **Description**: Give your API key a descriptive name.

When finished, click **Manage permissions** or** View and store credentials** (depending on which Harvest version you chose.)

After the the credential is created, click **Copy**, and paste the credentials in a secure location to provide to the integration later.

Click **I have stored the client credentials**.

**Note:**

- For Harvest v3, the client secret is shown only once. The client key remains visible.
- For Harvest v1/v2, the API key is shown only once and can't be viewed again after clicking I have stored the API key.

On the next screen, confirm or assign the required permissions (see sections below for more information). Click **Save** to complete setup.

### Update an existing Harvest API credential

To update a credential, use the same steps above from creating an API key (**Configure** > **Dev Center** > API **Credential Management**).

Hover over the credential you want to update and click **Edit** (pencil icon).

![](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/article_attachments/45999126085915)

If you're updating a Harvest v3 credential, click the **three-dot menu**, then click **Edit.**

![](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/article_attachments/48269408773915)

**Note:** Changing the permissions of an active API credential may affect any integrations that rely on it. To avoid disruptions, confirm required access with your development team or integration partner before making updates.

For security, share API keys or client credentials using a secure transfer method. Avoid sending them in plaintext emails.

#### Restrict IP access

Now in the **Edit** view of your credential, you can limit which IP addresses can use this credential by checking the **Restrict access to specific IP addresses** option.

![](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/article_attachments/45999107300379)

Enter trusted IP addresses or CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing) ranges (e.g., 203.0.113.0/24) into the **IP addresses allowed to access this credential** text area.

Only requests originating from the listed IPs will be allowed.

When finished, click **Save**.

#### Manage permissions or scopes

From within the same **Edit** view, there will be a **Manage permissions** or **Manage scopes** section where you can expand the available sections to select individual API endpoints and OAuth scopes.

![](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/article_attachments/45999126088859)

We recommend granting access only to the endpoints or scopes the integration requires. Work with your development or integration partner to determine what’s needed.

Click **Save** when finished.

#### Rotate the client secret

The client secret is used to authenticate API requests made through the Harvest V3 API (OAuth). Rotating the client secret generates a new credential and immediately invalidates the previous one.

This is accessed within the same *Manage Permissions* page and choosing the **Client secret** tab.

From there, click **Rotate secret**.

![](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/article_attachments/46600441464603)

Confirm in the dialog box that you want to **Rotate**. A new client secret will be generated and displayed.

Update any external systems or integrations using the previous client secret with the new value to prevent service disruptions.

Once rotated, the previous client secret can no longer be used to authenticate API requests.

### Revoke and re-enable a Harvest API credential

To revoke a credential and remove its access, go to **API Credential Management** once more.

Locate and hover over the credential you wish to revoke, click the **Revoke** icon ![](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/article_attachments/14515508074651) . (For Harvest v3 credentials, **Revoke** will be under the **three-dot menu**.)

![](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/article_attachments/45999126089371)

**Note:** Revoking an API key immediately removes access to the key for all users and integrations. Double-check that the API key you're revoking is the correct key.

Click **OK** to revoke the Harvest API key.

You can re-enable the credential later if needed.

To do so, locate and hover over the credential you wish to revoke and click the **Re-enable** icon ![](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/article_attachments/360081248232) . (For Harvest v3 credentials, click **Enable** under the **three-dot menu**.)

![](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/article_attachments/45999126093595)

Click **OK** to re-enable the Harvest API key.

### Export Harvest v1/v2 API credentials

Site Admins can export a list of all Harvest v1/v2 API credentials from the Dev Center as a CSV file. The export includes both active and inactive credentials, making it easier to audit existing API keys and track integrations, especially when preparing to migrate to Harvest v3.

To export credentials, navigate to the **Harvest v1/v2** tab in **API Credential Management** (Configure > Dev Center > API Credential Management).

Click **Export to CSV** in the top-right corner of the credentials table.

![](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/article_attachments/49673290904091)

The downloaded CSV file includes the following details for each credential:

- **Description:** The name assigned to the credential.
- **Status:** Whether the credential is active or inactive.
- **API key:** Masked — only the last 4 characters are shown, consistent with how keys appear in the Dev Center.
- **IP restrictions:** Any IP address restrictions applied to the credential.
- **Date created:** When the credential was created.
- **Last write date:** The most recent date the credential was used for a write operation.
- **Created by:** The name of the user who created the credential.

**Note:** Full API keys are never displayed or exported. Only the last 4 characters of each key are included in the CSV, consistent with how keys appear in the Dev Center.
